text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to Comcast's third quarter earnings conference
call. At this time, all participants are in listening-only mode. Please note this conference
call is being recorded. I will now turn the call over to Executive Vice President, Investor
Relations, Ms. Marci Reibacher. Please go ahead, Ms. Reibacher.
Thank you, Operator, and welcome, everyone. Joining us on today's call are Brian Roberts,
Mike Cavanaugh, Jason Armstrong, and Steve Crony.
I will now refer you to slide two of the presentation accompanying this call,
which can also be found on our Investor Relations website
and which contains our Safe Harbor disclaimer.
This conference call may include forward-looking statements
subject to certain risks and uncertainties.
In addition, during this call, we will refer to certain non-GAAP financial measures.
Please see our 8K and trending schedule issued earlier this morning
for the reconciliations of these non-GAAP financial measures to GAAP.
With that, I'll turn the call over to Mike.
Thanks, Marcy, and good morning, everyone.
Let me start with an update on the separation of NBCUniversal and Sky.
We are on track to complete the transaction by the middle of next year
and are well into the execution phase,
which includes building the standalone public company infrastructure.
And I'm pleased that Chris Halpin has joined us as NBCUniversal's CFO
as we announced earlier in the quarter.
While there is still significant work ahead,
we have a clear path to completion
and remain focused on creating two companies
with the strategic flexibility, financial strength,
and leadership to compete and grow independently.
And we have tremendous confidence
in the future of both companies.
Each has significant structural advantages,
a strong competitive position,
and substantial opportunities
for long-term growth and value creation.
I want to spend a few minutes highlighting what gives us that confidence.
At Comcast, we have been operating in an intensely competitive environment for some time.
Fixed wireless remains aggressive and continues to take share,
while fiber construction remains elevated with pockets of irrational pricing and promotional activity.
And while satellite is not yet a material factor,
we recognize the importance of anticipating emerging forms of competition
and positioning our business to respond as the market evolves.
This quarter's financial results reflect the significant investments we're making
to strengthen our competitive position, including fundamental changes to our pricing,
packaging, and overall customer proposition.
These investments are creating near-term financial pressure,
but we believe they're necessary to strengthen customer relationships
and position the business for return to growth over the long term.
Importantly, we have a set of structural advantages that are difficult to replicate.
Our focus is on fully capitalizing on these strengths through better execution and improved
customer experience and a more agile operating model.
Our capital-efficient network is the foundation of our best-in-class Wi-Fi experience and
the products and services we build around it.
That leadership continues to be validated by independent third-party testing with Xfinity
ranked number one nationally for consistent quality, download speed, and video experience,
and recognized for the most reliable Wi-Fi in our footprint. We're extending that leadership
through network virtualization and upgrades to multi-gigabit symmetrical speeds,
delivering even greater capacity, speed, and reliability at Attractive Economics.
We're bringing the same commitment to excellence to the customer experience.
The changes we've made are simplifying how customers interact with us
and making it easier to do business with Comcast.
We're seeing encouraging results with NPS improving both sequentially and year over year.
As we build on this progress by delivering greater value and a more seamless experience,
we believe we can better translate our product advantages into stronger customer loyalty and retention.
Wireless gives us a powerful competitive advantage in a market substantially larger than broadband.
We are the challenger, with a capital-A model that avoids the spectrum and network costs of traditional wireless operators
while leveraging our broadband and Wi-Fi leadership to deliver compelling value.
And with approximately 90% of Xfinity mobile traffic traveling over Wi-Fi,
We're able to leverage our existing infrastructure to deliver a great wireless product at highly attractive economics.
Importantly, Convergence also strengthens our core broadband business by deepening customer relationships, reducing churn, and increasing customer lifetime value.
And we're able to generate an attractive return across both businesses without meaningful incremental capital investment.
We believe we have the best hand in convergence
with significant opportunity to expand our position in wireless.
And in business services, we've built a highly profitable business
generating nearly $6 billion annually in EBITDA
with substantial opportunity ahead, particularly in enterprise,
where we're taking share in a market dominated by legacy providers
by delivering more flexible, integrated solutions
to increasingly complex customer needs.
Our network and established small business presence provide a strong foundation, but our talented sales force is a real differentiator.

Combined with our expanding portfolio of advanced networking, security, and managed solutions, we're deepening customer relationships, capturing more of their technology spending, and extending our reach well beyond our network footprint.
We're already seeing the results with solid enterprise revenue growth and increasing adoption of advanced services.
But these advantages alone aren't enough.
The competitive environment demands that we execute at a higher level, move faster, and operate more efficiently.
That's exactly where the team, working closely with Michael Angelakis as he prepares to become Comcast CEO next year, is focused.
We're taking decisive steps to change how we operate, structurally improve our cost base, and create greater capacity to invest in growth.
Building on the organizational changes Steve has made, including strategic external hires,
we've embarked on the most significant operating and cost transformation in our company's history,
with an opportunity we believe will ultimately amount to billions of dollars over time.
This goes well beyond cost savings.
We're challenging established ways of working and redesigning how we make decisions, allocate resources,
and run the business to create a more agile, efficient organization
that can compete more effectively and invest more decisively in growth.
Taken together, these advantages and the significant changes underway
give us confidence in Comcast's ability to compete more effectively
and create meaningful value for shareholders.
Turning to content and experiences,
we're equally confident in the future of NBC, Universal, and Sky.
We have an exceptional portfolio of businesses, a strong competitive position, and significant opportunities for long-term growth and value creation.
And there are several reasons why we believe we are so well-positioned.
First, we operate an integrated model across some of the most attractive and fastest-growing segments of media and entertainment.
At the center are our industry-leading film and television studios,
home to iconic franchises that fuel creativity and innovation across our businesses.
We're also one of only two globally-scaled theme park businesses,
welcoming millions of guests annually and bringing our stories and franchises to life through immersive experiences.
Our media business, anchored by NBC and Peacock, reaches more than 100 million U.S. households each quarter,

while Sky extends our scale internationally through a leading European media platform with deep direct-to-consumer relationships and premium sports, news, and entertainment offerings, further strengthened by the proposed acquisition of ITV.
Finally and importantly, we also have limited exposure to areas facing greater secular pressure, including linear pay TV networks.
Second, we are a natural home to the world's best creators, talent, IP, and fandoms.
We attract the world's leading creators and storytellers.
Across film and television, we've built an extraordinary collection of enduring franchises
from Jurassic, Despicable Me and Minions, Shrek and Fast and Furious,
to Law & Order, One Chicago, Love Island, and Dayline.
This extends to live programming, where we have one of the strongest sports portfolios in the industry,
including the NFL, NBA, and WNBA, MLB, Big Ten, Olympics, and Premier League.
Beyond sports, iconic live events such as Saturday Night Live, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade,
and Bravo's signature programming bring audiences together at scale.
Creators, talent, and partners choose to work with us because they understand and value our ability to develop IP,
build fandoms, and extend successful franchises across film, television, streaming, live programming, and theme parks.
Third, our open architecture approach is a real competitive advantage.
Fragmentation and diversity are the reality of the media and entertainment landscape.
No one company can serve every consumer with everything.
In that context, we believe being a closed shop or walled garden serves both the company and consumers poorly.
Our core strategy is to combine our exceptional content and distribution with select partners and third-party IP to reach audiences wherever they choose to engage.
You can see this in our recently announced bundle with YouTube, which will expand Peacock's reach and accessibility while introducing our content and brands to a new and younger audience.
It's also reflected in our theme park partnerships with franchises like Nintendo, Pokemon, and Harry Potter, where we bring some of the world's most beloved IP to life through immersive experiences.
Finally, we intend to enter this next chapter with a strong investment-grade balance sheet,
enabling continued investment in our brands, content, technology, and experiences,
while preserving the financial capacity to capitalize on future opportunities.
Combined with our diversified revenue streams across advertising, subscriptions, licensing, and experiences,
we believe we are positioned to drive long-term growth and value creation.
Now reflecting on this quarter, in media, Peacock was profitable for the second consecutive quarter and ended the period with 48 million subscribers.
We also delivered the highest rated Spanish language World Cup in U.S. history across Telemundo and Peacock.
In studios, Universal reached another significant milestone this quarter,
becoming the first studio this year to suppress $5 billion at the global box office,
led by an exceptional slate that included The Odyssey,
which became the highest-grossing film in the studio's history.
Finally, in parks, we remain confident in the long-term outlook for this business.
Our powerful IP differentiated attractions and world-class destinations
position us well for long-term growth.
While we continue to see near-term demand pressure across portions of the parks business,
including in Orlando and certain international markets,
We view these trends as temporary rather than structural due to the confluence of a few factors.
In addition to the macroeconomic and geopolitical headwinds we have referenced in the past,
we believe two other factors have contributed to this recent softness.
First, we believe competitors were quicker to anticipate and recognize softness in demand
and adapt their marketing strategies.
And second, we continue to work through capacity challenges and ride throughput at EPIC, given the complexities of opening the most technologically advanced theme park ever built.
We are taking action to address both of these challenges.
Additionally, we are investing in our management team.
Earlier this month, we announced a new chief brand and commercial officer, Luke Bondar, who joins from United Airlines and started this week.
And we just announced that Randy Culbertson, who until recently served as NBCUniversal's CFO, will also be joining Universal Destinations and Experiences as Chief Business Officer.
The fundamentals of the business remain strong.
In Orlando, attendance, guest spending, and overall financial performance remain materially above where they were two years ago, and guest satisfaction continues to rise.
Looking ahead, we expect performance to strengthen as we move through 2027 with a return to growth in the second half of the year.
While the path may not be linear, particularly given the broader operating environment, we remain confident in the underlying strength of the business.
And in closing, as we prepare for our next chapter as an independent public company, we believe NBCUniversal is exceptionally well positioned for long-term growth and value creation.
With that, I'll hand it over to Jason.
Thanks, Mike, and good morning, everyone.
I'll start with an overview of our consolidated results before turning the performance of our businesses.
On a pro forma basis, third quarter revenue was flat, while adjusted EBITDA increased approximately 1%.
Adjusted earnings per share were $1.07, and we generated a strong $4.2 billion in free cash flow in the quarter.
Let me now get into more detail on our businesses, starting with connectivity and platforms.
Mike outlined the scale of the transformation ahead and the significant opportunity we see
to strengthen our competitive position and unlock the full potential of this business.
I want to build on that by highlighting three priorities where we're taking decisive action
to change how we operate, structurally improve our cost base, and create greater capacity
to invest in growth.
First, we are fundamentally redesigning our organization.
We've already made important leadership changes across customer experience, growth, and marketing.
We're simplifying our organizational structure to move faster, improve execution, and operate more efficiently.
As part of this transformation, we do expect to take a significant charge in the fourth quarter.
I'll have more on that in a minute.
Second, we're accelerating our technology transformation, product innovation, and AI adoption.
We're bringing in new technology leadership to increase the pace of innovation.
AI is already embedded across our network to optimize performance,
and we're expanding its application across customer experience
through partnerships with Sierra and Cresta.
These capabilities are central to our new operating model,
enabling us to bring products to market faster,
simplifying customer interactions,
and deliver a better experience more efficiently.
We've already reduced customer service contact rates by roughly 20%
and eliminated more than 30 million service interactions year-to-date versus the prior year.
And as personal AI agents reshape how consumers discover, purchase, and manage services,
we're positioning Comcast to capitalize on that shift.
In a consumer-agentic world, it's logical that differentiation is a key to success,
and we've got a culture of innovation pointed at just that.
Third, we're sharpening our focus on retention,
delivering more value and giving customers more reasons to stay with us.
We've reduced historical pain points around promotional pricing expirations.
We've invested to increase awareness of our wireless product,
and now we'll push wireless relationships even deeper.
Our free line strategy has been a key tool in building awareness,
but we're now positioned to push further on multi-line customers,
premium plans, and new device offerings,
which meaningfully reduce churn and strengthen the overall relationship.
And we'll continue to innovate with new products and features like Xfinity Shield, which we launched this quarter.
We see home security, protection, and cyber as a category we can reposition for the benefit of the broader relationship.
While significant work remains, we're confident these actions will strengthen our competitive position,
improve operating efficiency, and unlock greater earnings and cash flow potential for the long term.
Between the internal and external changes that are underway,
It is our intention to provide more context early next year, with Michael Angelakis joining us at that point to discuss in detail.
Now let me turn to the results of the quarter.
Our performance continues to reflect the financial impact of the go-to-market changes we've made over the past year,
including simpler pricing and packaging, an improved customer experience, and deeper convergence through wireless.
As expected, these investments continued to pressure near-term financial results, with revenue declining 2.6% and EBITDA declining 4.4%.
But as the quarter demonstrated, we're beginning to see modest improvement as we lap our initial investments and convert free wireless lines into paid relationships.
In the third quarter, year-over-year declines in Convergence ARPA and Broadband ARPU narrowed sequentially by 190 basis points respectively,
while the connectivity and platforms EBITDA decline narrowed by 140 basis points.
We're also seeing encouraging operational indicators.
MPS improved again year over year, reflecting stronger customer perceptions of our service experience,
and approximately 45% of our broadband base is now on gig plus speed tiers,
up nearly 10 percentage points from a year ago.
Looking ahead, we expect further slight improvement in these underlying financial trends in the fourth quarter,
even as we continue migrating broadband customers to our new pricing and packaging and offering free wireless lines.
Convergence remains central to our strategy, with a focus on increasing wireless penetration to grow the value of our broadband relationships.
Convergence revenue and ARPA remain key measures of our progress.
In the quarter, convergence revenue declined 2% and convergence ARPA declined 0.5%,
reflecting continued pressure on broadband revenue, partially offset by nearly 15% growth in wireless service revenue.
Turning to customer trends, we lost 144,000 broadband subscribers and added 368,000 net wireless lines in the quarter.
As Mike highlighted, competition remains intense, with particularly aggressive fiber promotions in certain markets during the quarter.
At the same time, we had a higher-than-typical volume of customers facing pricing transitions across our legacy broadband customer base.
Together, these dynamics contributed to higher churn and year-over-year pressure on both broadband and wireless subscriber trends.
In response, as I mentioned earlier, we've been refining our offers and retention strategies to better manage these transitions and strengthen customer retention.
on wireless we're continuing to make progress converting free lines into paying relationships
and moving customers towards higher value plans approximately half of our residential post-paid
phone connects continued to come from customers taking a free line and we're now converting 70
of those free lines into paying relationships this is an important validation of our strategy
to build a wireless awareness move customers into paying relationships and drive upsell into
multi-line and premium wireless. On that note, we're also seeing encouraging progress at the
premium end of the market. Premium unlimited plans represented approximately 40 percent
of our postpaid phone connects, up from 30 percent last quarter, and premium customers
now account for roughly 25 percent of our phone base. This improving mix, combined with our
opportunity to add more lines per household, positions us to deepen customer relationships
and support convergence ARPA growth over time.
We ended the quarter with 10.6 million total wireless lines,
up 18% year-over-year and 40% over two years.
That represents nearly 18% penetration of our residential broadband base
and approximately 7% of the total addressable wireless lines in our footprint.
Turning to business services, revenue increased 2.7% and EBITDA grew 1.7%.

In small business, revenue was essentially flat, and while we were seeing ongoing competitive pressure, we are offsetting this through uptake of additional products and services, including mobile, wireless connect for backup connectivity, and security solutions like SecurityEdge, together helping us increase the value of our existing customer relationships.
Enterprise Solutions remains the primary growth driver within business services,
supported by healthy demand for advanced connectivity, managed networking, and security solutions.
Moving to content and experiences, there are a few items I'd like to highlight.
Starting with media, revenue increased 13%, and EBITDA grew more than $500 million to $769 million,
driven by strong growth at Peacock.
The World Cup on Telemundo and Peacock aired across both second and third quarters and
generated incremental advertising of $224 million in the third quarter and $664 million
in total.
Peacock was the primary driver of media results, delivering its second consecutive quarter
of profitability with $261 million of EBITDA, a $478 million improvement year over year.
Peacock revenue increased 34%, reflecting strong growth in both distribution and advertising.
Distribution revenue increased 44%, driven by higher sub-fees and growth in paid subscribers,
which increased by $7 million year-over-year.
Importantly, paid subscribers remained stable sequentially, demonstrating strong retention
even as we began implementing a price increase earlier in the quarter.
And advertising revenue grew 23%, driven by the FIFA World Cup, Love Island, which was the number one streaming show this summer, and Five Star Weekend, our top scripted series.
At studios, revenue declined 1%, reflecting the timing of lower-margin television licensing deals.
However, theatrical revenue increased 77%, contributing to 19% growth in studios EBITDA.
Our film slate delivered exceptional results, led by Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey,
which generated $1.8 billion in worldwide box office to become Universal's biggest film ever,
and Obsession, which set a new box office record for Focus Features
and became the top-grossing original film of 2026.
Turning to theme parks, revenue declined 4% and EBITDA declined 17%,
primarily reflecting continued pressure in Orlando and Japan.
In Orlando, the softness that began in June continued through the third quarter
and was the primary driver of weaker financial results.
And in Japan, China-related travel restrictions continued to weigh on attendance and financial performance.
Looking ahead, we expect to begin lapping the initial pressure in Japan in the fourth quarter,
while Hollywood should benefit from the recent opening of the new Fast and Furious coaster.
However, softer demand and difficult comparisons in Orlando
are expected to remain headwinds to overall theme park results in the fourth quarter.
Now let me wrap up with free cash flow and capital allocation.
But before I do that, as I said earlier,
we expect to have a significant charge in the fourth quarter
related mostly to our transformation efforts,
and I would quantify that at over $1 billion.
In the quarter, we delivered $4.2 billion of free cash flow,
reflecting the underlying strength and cash-generating capacity of our businesses,
as well as favorable timing impacts that we expect to reverse in the fourth quarter.
We paid $1.2 billion in dividends to shareholders.
As previously announced, we paused our share repurchases as of July 1st
and expect that pause to remain in place at least through the separation,
as we ensure both businesses are positioned with strong balance sheets and investment-grade ratings.
Our priority is to bribe the financial flexibility for both companies
to pursue their respective growth strategies for the long term.
With that, let me turn it back to Marcy for Q&A.
Marcy.
Thanks, Jason.
Operator, please open the call for Q&A.
Thank you.
We'll now begin the question and answer session.
If you have a question, please press star and the number one on your touchtone phone.
If you wish to be removed from the queue, please press star and the number two.
If you're using a speakerphone, you may need to pick up the handset first
before pressing the numbers.
Once again, if there are any questions, please press star,
the number one on your touchtone phone.
Our first question is coming from Craig Moffitt from Moffitt & Nathanson.
Your line is now live.
Hi, thank you.
A question for Jason, I guess.
Jason, about a month ago, you talked about irrational competition.
You mentioned it a short time ago in your prepared remarks as well.
Just in the past, I guess, two weeks or so, we've seen AT&T raise prices pretty considerably.
We've seen just about everybody now start to raise prices in broadband.
I know it's very early days, but have those price changes that have happened in the market
had any impact yet on the kind of results that you're seeing
as the competition, I guess, to use your words,
maybe becomes a little less irrational?
Hey, thanks, Craig. It's Jason.
I'll start, and Steve can chime in as well.
I think if you rewind the clock, that's right.
We were at a conference in September
and highlighted what we thought was some irrational competition
that we started to see at the end of the second quarter,
saw sort of consistently through the third quarter,
And, you know, I would tell you there's still pockets of it out there, certainly in the fourth quarter.
I would generally characterize the environment as it's been competitive all year.
It's been more competitive in the second half than it has been in the first half for sure.
As we step back, you know, the irrational comment was, you know, we know what the cost of building fiber is.
We obviously do a lot of overbuilding and deploy a lot of this ourselves.
So it's, you know, at $1,500 plus per home, getting more expensive with construction costs up.
As you get into more suburban and rural areas, the underlying cost structure of deploying fiber going up against, you know,
what we saw is $30 to $40 pricing, you know, in specific markets in the third quarter.
As we look at the return profile of that, you know, to us, that is a rational competition.
A lot of people have asked us the subsequent question, you know, on our wireless strategy
and sort of pointed the finger back at us and said, well, you guys are offering free wireless lines.
Isn't that irrational?
I would just point out we actually think we're competing very rationally in wireless.
When we offer a free wireless line, it is against zero capital deployed.
We don't have spectrum.
We don't have towers.
Our model is an MVNO model.
The extent people are using our network, engaging with us, they're converting into paying subscribers
within a year to a very rational price point, we think, and then our goal is obviously to
upsell them over time.
So I won't call the last couple of weeks as a real change in trend.
I think it continues to be very competitive, but Steve can fill in some of the details
as well.
Yeah, as we really assess the marketplace,
we maintain that gig pricing at $30 to $40, in some cases even less,
is going to be really hard to sustain.
So as we assess the overall environment,
we're going to continue to compete aggressively,
but we're going to compete with discipline
and really focus on differentiating our products,
adding value through deepening our customer relationships,
and continuing to provide a great customer experience
so we're not giving our customers a reason to leave.
Thanks, Craig. Operator, next question, please.
Certainly. Next question is coming from Michael Rollins from Citi. Your line is now live.
Thanks, and good morning. So, keeping on the theme of broadband and convergence,
curious, as you're at an 18% penetration of your residential broadband customers,
is there a tipping point that we should all keep in mind that you can get to
where that then starts to show a meaningfully better performance in converged revenue
and particularly in broadband as you keep building that scale of the bundle.
Yeah, so I'll jump in there.
We feel mobile remains a tremendous growth opportunity for us.
It's a capital-like model, leverages our existing customer broadband base.
We have Wi-Fi leadership that helps with the offload,
which enables us to create a great value proposition that's resonating with our customers.
As you stated, at 18% penetration, 7% of lines, there's a huge upside there.
But, you know, similar to broadband, it remains competitive, that marketplace.
And we saw switching activities slow down a bit in the quarter, you know,
with some of the new product offerings in the marketplace,
some of the new converged offerings in the marketplace.
But with that being said, we still added, you know, close to 370,000 lines.
And in 2026, it will be our best mobile line net ad year in the company's history.
And we look at it strategically how we're attacking the market.
Our free wireless offer has delivered on the intended objectives.
You know, first and foremost, it rallied the organization and really focused the organization on mobile and the value of convergence.
Secondarily, it increased awareness with our customer base, which was hugely important,
and that has since driven adoption and expanded the wireless base.
And the great news is 70% of those customers are rolling to paid.
And when we look at the dynamic of those customers, porting is very similar to a paid customer.
Usage is similar to a paid customer.
Our premium mix is actually a bit higher in that free line base as we've really leaned into the premium segment.
Average lines per account are a bit less, but the good news there is we continue to see those lines per account increase over time.
So really, really pleased with that strategy.
Then as I touched on, you know, leaning into the premium strategy,
if you go back a year or so ago, we weren't even competing in that marketplace.
We're now connecting at about 40% attach and 25% of our base as a premium product,
and that's really improving the quality of our mobile customer base, which is great.
And now we're really focusing on investing in multi-line attach
and further deepening our relationships, which is hugely important to us.
So, you know, I think, once again, back to that 7% number,
We have a long runway ahead of us, and we really like the benefits we see in the broadband base when we do attach mobile.
Thanks, Mike.
Operator, next question, please.
Our next question is coming from John Hudlick from UBS.
Your line is now live.
Great.
Thank you.
Maybe a couple questions on Peacock for Mike.
Obviously, strong profitability this quarter.
Do you expect that to continue on a quarterly basis going forward?
Anything you can tell us about sort of longer-term target margins?
And then should we see an uptick in the overall profitability of the Peacock business
when the YouTube agreement kicks in early next year?
Thanks.
Thanks, Jonathan.
So we're very pleased, obviously, with what we've been seeing of late with Peacock,
you know, holding our subs at $48 million this quarter.
As Jason said, that's on the back of a successfully landed price increase
that was so far successfully landed late in the summer, and another profitable quarter.
I think the quarters ahead, you get lumpy depending on when rights kick in for different properties,
so not so much focused on profitability quarter by quarter,
but I think if you start looking back, you know, prospective years and annual basis on a look-forward
or look-back basis, I expect us to continue to drive profitability in the business.
for all the reasons we've been focused on and talking about.
It's a great value.
It's got an unbelievable portfolio of sports
and successful path on bringing in pay-one movies from Universal,
plus library, plus originals.
It's a formula that we like what we see.
It works in concert with what we're doing at NBC and Universal Studios,
so it's a strategy that works well for us.
And I think the thing that you mentioned separately was YouTube.
So let me just come back to the stage that we've been through.
I think we just passed our sixth anniversary of Peacock.
And we did quite a good job, I would say, in the early years,
focusing on building primarily direct-to-consumer customer base at high ARPUs.
And that's been what you can see when you look at our results versus others.
We always thought there would be a point, and we're at that point recently,
where bundling with others was going to be a part of the strategy for Peacock.
And it goes back to my earlier comments about being open architecture
and working with other partners in the ecosystem in a variety of different ways,
and certainly having Peacock bundled with others is part of that.
You've seen us do things with Apple, Amazon, and Walmart, working on things bundled with others.
But let me talk about YouTube for a second, which is going to be a bundled offering
of YouTube Premium with Peacock, another step in this strategy I just described.
And what makes YouTube particularly attractive is that we already have a significant amount
of NBC clips and content consumed there.
So there's an awareness of that.
But those viewers are typically, while familiar with our brands and franchises, they're not
currently Peacock subscribers.
So this bundle will give us another opportunity to reach a younger and incremental audience,
and in concert with the YouTube main fandoms, drive greater engagement around our content.
So we feel very good about the strategy there.
And with YouTube as well, there was more to it than just the bundle with Peacock.
We extended our linear portfolio distribution deal with YouTube TV.
expanded some aspects of our advertising relationships with them
and are looking at some international opportunities as well.
So we're very excited about the relationship with YouTube,
and we'll talk more as we get into the new year when we start to get ready to talk to investors
about our excitement for the new NBCUniversal.
But, yes, to your point, I think we are interested in doing this with others as well.
Different bundles will be different for different types of partners.
but we're looking to do exactly what I said,
which is make them additive to the business we've already built,
be careful about cannibalization of our existing business,
and come up with win-win solutions given the power of our content that's embedded in Peacock,
and that's resonating well in the marketplace.
Thanks, John.
Operator, next question, please.
Our next question is coming from Jessica Referlick from Bank of America.
Your line is now live.
Thank you.
I guess just maybe staying on NBCU, but moving on to advertising,
can you give us an update on what you're seeing in the overall market,
any flow-through benefits from the World Cup,
and just a follow-up on Peacock.
I asked this question in court, but do you feel like you have enough scale?
And are there any other – you've obviously just talked
through the YouTube premium bundle.
Any thoughts on other partnerships or bundling,
which seems like the direction the industry is headed anyway?
Hey, Jessica.
So on advertising, I'd say the environment when you normalize for World Cup
and game counts in this quarter versus others say that the overall environment is stable,
relatively stable, and mixed in categories with some tech growth offsetting weakness
in consumer-driven categories, but overall pretty stable
and strength, obviously, around live programming and sports,
and so our portfolio performs very well in that regard.
I mean, in terms of scale, I think as I just commented on Peacock,
we have a strategy of bundling with others as well as building
and investing in our own direct consumer, and that's working,
and we are open to doing more of the same,
and it's key to the fundamental strategy of the new NBC Universal.
But when they ask the question of do we have scale, I mean, I'd like to, you know,
just make the point that we have scale, as I talked about last time and earlier in these remarks.
When you think about scale in terms of our position in businesses, you know,
we are the number two player, one of two in the global theme parks business,
